solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Reportedly where one might see vinegar everywhere

indicators.note: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so we go by how the words sound when spoken

parts.note: vinegar is splashed on fish and chips, and plaice is a flatfish often served that way

explanation.surface: A spilt bottle of vinegar has gone everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Vinegar goes on fish in a British chip shop, so it would be all over the plaice; plaice is a common flatfish, and it sounds exactly like place.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means scattered in every direction or found in all locations, matching the adverb exactly.

clue.text: A long lead for hounds?

parts.note: surface reading: an extended leash for walking a pack of dogs
setter's reading: the letter that leads the word hounds, written out at length as a word rather than a single character

explanation.surface: A dog walker wants an extra-long leash for the pack.
explanation.walkthrough: Lead means the first letter of hounds, and long means that letter spelt out in full as its name.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of the eighth letter of the alphabet, spelt as a word, is the opening letter of hounds.

clue.text: Drink, spirit mostly, that's kept in a fancy wagon

indicators.note: what is kept in something sits inside it, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a Lambo, short for Lamborghini, is a flashy car

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: rum is a spirit; the last letter goes
sc. is the abbreviation of scilicet, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: Someone sips spirits kept in a smart drinks trolley.
explanation.walkthrough: RU plus SC go inside LAMBO to make LAMBRUSCO. 'That's' is the Latin scilicet, abbreviated sc., a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambrusco is a sparkling red wine from northern Italy, so it is a kind of alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: See story about one covering boat race in Docklands?

definitions.text: one covering boat race in Docklands?

parts.note: v. is the abbreviation of vide, Latin for see

indicators.note: to go about is to turn round, so the letters are read the other way

parts.note: a lie is a made-up story

explanation.surface: Look out for a story about a rowing race held in London's Docklands.
explanation.walkthrough: Boat race is Cockney rhyming slang for face, and Docklands in east London is Cockney country; so the definition is something covering a face.
explanation.definitionFit: A veil is a piece of fabric worn to cover or conceal the face, as at a wedding.

clue.text: Skunk perhaps behind low-quality paper plant

indicators.note: what is behind comes after, so the two pieces sit one after the other

parts.note: a rag is a disparaging word for a cheap newspaper
skunk is a strong strain of cannabis, which is called weed

explanation.surface: A skunk lurks behind a pile of cheap newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: Skunk looks like the animal, but it is a potent kind of cannabis; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragweed is a weedy flowering species whose pollen causes hay fever, so it is a botanical specimen.

clue.text: Home somewhat overshadowed by Balmoral?

indicators.note: something overshadowed is covered over from above, so one piece is wrapped by another

parts.note: a balmoral is a Scottish brimless cap
somewhat means a bit

explanation.surface: A house stands in the shadow of the royal estate at Balmoral.
explanation.walkthrough: Balmoral looks like the royal castle in Scotland, but a balmoral is also a flat bonnet; HAT goes round A BIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitat is the natural environment where an animal or plant normally lives, its dwelling place.

clue.text: A part of church that liberal's left, possibly

parts.note: per means a, as in so much a head

indicators.note: something that has left is gone, so that letter departs from the word

parts.note: the chancel is the area round the altar
L is the abbreviation for liberal

explanation.surface: A liberal has walked out of a section of the church.
explanation.walkthrough: Per and a are interchangeable in prices (five pounds per head, five pounds a head); CHANCEL then loses its L.
explanation.definitionFit: Perchance is an archaic or literary word meaning perhaps or by some chance.

clue.text: A flash republican covering up university affair

parts.note: taken as written
a mo is a moment, a flash

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means read from bottom to top, so the pair is turned over

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for republican
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A showy Republican hushes up a scandal involving a university.
explanation.walkthrough: R sitting over U gives RU, and up turns it to UR in a down answer. 'Flash' is a noun meaning an instant, not an adjective meaning showy.
explanation.definitionFit: Amour is French borrowed into English for a love affair, especially a secret one.

clue.text: You might say the Dutch are ones up for change

indicators.note: letters up for change are open to being altered, so they get rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these three words are the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that the Dutch are always keen on reform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ones up for change' reads like a description of the Dutch, but it is the anagram; 'You might say' signals the definition is by example.
explanation.definitionFit: The people of the Netherlands belong to the continent of Europe, so they are one instance of the wider group.

clue.text: Agency work's attractive if a bit short on time

indicators.note: being short on something means lacking it, so a letter is missing from the word

parts.note: tempting means alluring, attractive
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Working through an agency appeals, if you don't mind long hours being cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: TEMPTING loses one T to leave the answer; it does not matter which T goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Temping is doing short-term jobs found through an employment agency, standing in for permanent staff.

clue.text: Type of jacket Barnet tradesman picked up

indicators.note: to pick up a sound is to hear it, so we go by what the ear catches

parts.note: Barnet Fair is Cockney rhyming slang for hair, and the tradesman who cuts it is a barber

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper from Barnet in north London hears about a jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: Barnet looks like the London borough, but it is rhyming slang for hair, via Barnet Fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbour is a British brand of waxed cotton outdoor coat, so its name denotes a style of outerwear.

clue.text: Rent's more expensively priced, so I'm told

indicators.note: being told something means hearing it spoken, so the sound is what counts

parts.note: a pricier item has a higher price

explanation.surface: A tenant has heard the rent is going up.
explanation.walkthrough: Higher and the answer sound alike in most accents.
explanation.definitionFit: To hire something is to pay for its temporary use, exactly as you rent a car or a hall.

clue.text: Walk in America and berate path in bad condition

indicators.note: something in bad condition is broken down, so the letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: the fodder letters

explanation.surface: A walker in the States complains about a footpath in poor repair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Walk' here is the slang sense, to go free from a charge, not to stroll; the phrase is American.
explanation.definitionFit: In American slang, to walk is to be acquitted, and to beat the rap is to escape conviction for a crime.

clue.text: Will possibly split by a good man and a bad one

indicators.note: a thing split by something is broken open with that thing inside it

parts.note: William Shakespeare is known as the Bard
taken as written
a saint, abbreviated ST, is a good man

explanation.surface: A will is contested between a decent man and a villain.
explanation.walkthrough: Will looks like a legal document, but it is Shakespeare; 'one' in the definition stands for man.
explanation.definitionFit: Bastard is a coarse insult for a nasty or unpleasant man, a villain.

clue.text: A berk drunk on table topless gets smashed easily

definitions.note: means 'can be smashed easily', an adjective once 'gets' links it

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece on another sits above it
someone drunk staggers about, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the fodder letters

indicators.note: without a top, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: taken as written, then its first letter goes

explanation.surface: An idiot drinking topless on a table gets very drunk with ease.
explanation.walkthrough: A berk is a fool in British slang. 'Smashed' suggests drunk, but here it means broken.
explanation.definitionFit: Something breakable is fragile and can be shattered without much force.

clue.text: What might ruin mother in a tribunal battle

indicators.note: one thing in another is placed inside it

parts.note: taken as written
a tribunal is a kind of court
gin is nicknamed mother's ruin

explanation.surface: A mother's reputation could be wrecked in a fight before a tribunal.
explanation.walkthrough: Mother's ruin is an old British nickname for gin, from its role in the 18th-century gin craze.
explanation.definitionFit: Agincourt was the 1415 clash in which Henry V's English army defeated the French.

clue.text: Land fish around section of the Thames endlessly

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: tuna is a fish

indicators.note: without an end, the word loses its last letter

parts.note: the Isis is the name of the Thames as it flows through Oxford; it drops its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone casts a line along a stretch of the Thames for a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: Land is a noun for a country here, not the verb to catch a fish, which the surface pushes.
explanation.definitionFit: Tunisia is a North African country, and land is a common crossword word for a nation.

clue.text: Relief maybe created by overturned cup result

indicators.note: things overturned are tipped over and jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder letters

explanation.surface: Fans feel relief after a cup tie result is reversed.
explanation.walkthrough: Relief looks like a feeling, but it is the art term for carving raised from a flat background.
explanation.definitionFit: A relief is one form of carved or modelled artwork, so it is an example of the wider art.

clue.text: Leader of evil movement creates strong feeling

indicators.note: the leader is the one at the front, so only the first letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter
motion is movement

explanation.surface: The head of a sinister campaign stirs up passions.
explanation.walkthrough: Leader looks like a person in charge, but it only takes the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An emotion is an intense state of mind such as love, anger or fear.

clue.text: Toff with trapped wind seen by island capital

indicators.note: seen by means next to, so the pieces sit side by side
something trapped is held inside, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: a nob is a posh, upper-class person
air is wind
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A posh chap suffering from wind is spotted beside an island's main city.
explanation.walkthrough: Toff and nob are both British slang for an upper-class person.
explanation.definitionFit: Nairobi is the seat of government and largest city of Kenya.

clue.text: Ways a heavenly body has earl in its thrall

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to have something in one's grip is to hold it, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: Venus is a planet
E is the abbreviation for earl

explanation.surface: A goddess of love has a nobleman under her spell.
explanation.walkthrough: Venus is both the planet and the goddess of love, which is why the earl is in her thrall.
explanation.definitionFit: Avenues are routes or means of approach, as in exploring every avenue to a solution.

clue.text: As a Kent prison closing early, run to get inside

indicators.note: getting inside means going into something, so one piece enters another
closing early means stopping before the end, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: taken as written
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
Kent is a county in South East England
nick is British slang for a jail

explanation.surface: A prison in Kent shuts early, so someone runs to get in.
explanation.walkthrough: As looks like the conjunction, but it is the chemical symbol of the element; Kent, a county, lies in the SE of England.
explanation.definitionFit: As is the chemical symbol for the toxic element number 33 in the periodic table.

clue.text: Is thickset criminal more vulgar than anyone else?

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked, so the letters are bent out of shape

parts.note: the fodder letters

explanation.surface: Is a stocky crook the crudest of them all?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' reads as a noun for a stocky crook, but it is an adjective signalling the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitsch describes tasteless, showy art or style, so the superlative means the most garish of all.

clue.text: Large piece of egg found underneath bird book

indicators.note: in a down answer, what is underneath comes lower, so the pieces follow one after another

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
L is the abbreviation for large

indicators.note: a piece is just one small bit, so a single letter, the first, is kept

parts.note: the opening letter

explanation.surface: A big chunk of eggshell lies under a bird's nest.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a large piece of egg; actually large and the piece of egg are separate letters under the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A title is a published work, as in a publisher's list of new titles.

clue.text: Parrot and primate seen close to reindeer

parts.note: an ape is a primate

indicators.note: the close is the end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter

explanation.surface: A parrot and a monkey are spotted near a reindeer.
explanation.walkthrough: Parrot looks like the bird but is a noun for a mimic; 'seen' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An aper is someone who mimics others, just as a parrot repeats what it hears.

clue.text: Actively oppose taking fifth examination

indicators.note: taking something away removes it, here the letter in the fifth slot

parts.note: to resist is to actively oppose

explanation.surface: A student fights against sitting a fifth test.
explanation.walkthrough: RESIST loses its fifth letter. A resit is a British term for retaking a failed exam.
explanation.definitionFit: A resit is a second attempt at a test after failing the first, so it is an exam.

clue.text: Hard to avoid Escort or a person on horse, say

indicators.note: to avoid something is to keep it out, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: an usher escorts people to their seats
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A rider tries to steer clear of an escort on horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: Horse is slang for heroin, so a person on horse is a drug taker; 'say' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A user is slang for someone who takes illegal drugs, of which heroin is one instance.

clue.text: Not all grab at tutor's Italian chopped herbs

indicators.note: not all of the words is used, only a run of letters sitting inside them

parts.note: the run of letters spans these words

explanation.surface: Someone half-heartedly snatches at a tutor's plate of Italian herbs.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of grab through at into the start of tutor's.
explanation.definitionFit: Battuto is an Italian cooking base of finely minced herbs and vegetables, like a soffritto before frying.

clue.text: Great meals, but not any drinks put on by hotel

parts.note: not any means none, no

indicators.note: something put on by another is taken in by it, so one piece goes within

parts.note: sups are sips or drinks
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A hotel lays on fine dinners but no drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: Nosh is British slang for food, and a nosh-up is a big, satisfying feed.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosh-up is a large, hearty meal, informal British slang for a feast.

clue.text: I head to town on tail of oddly eccentric ruler

indicators.note: done oddly means done in a strange way, so the letters fall into an unusual order
the head is the front, so only the first letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter
the remaining fodder letters

explanation.surface: An odd monarch announces his journey into town.
explanation.walkthrough: I looks like the pronoun, but in physics I is the symbol for current.
explanation.definitionFit: In equations the symbol I stands for the flow of charge, measured in amperes.
